Incredibly unsubtle, anti-AI/exploitative tech resource manager/idle clicker that loses momentum about ~30m-1h before the ending stretch; it doesn't really justify using AI assets for the dataset from one of the biggest offenders of reckless, forced AI expansion IRL (NVIDIA) since the faces will stop being relevant to the plot about 10 minutes into a playthrough once auto mode's used — an actual artist or even stock images could've easily been used in this regard.

I'd say the only positives are the visuals, which do a better job of emulating the 90s desktop vibes than other games I've seen like Hypnospace Outlaw, and the soundtrack. Pretty much everything else has been explored in much better ways.

When I saw this game, it was love at first sight but now I'm split.

[b]PROS[/b]
[list]
[*]Its graphics, and ambiance as a whole, gave me a rush of nostalgia ; 
[*]I love the  concept of the game (AI and its abuse) ;
[*]The voicemails you receive through the game go well with the concept of the game ;
[*]You can somehow feel the dev's passion and love for their game.
[/list]

[b]PROBLEM[/b]
[list]
[*][b]No manual save nor frequent autosave ![/b]
[/list]
No manual save would not be a huge problem had a frequent autosave been implemented. Saves only occur when you reach specific levels. I read that there was a way to create manual saves later in the game but it seems it costs money and its costs increase with every use. As a consequence, progressing in the game is in itself a source of stress as you never know if you will reach another save and may have to continue playing to reach it even if you want to stop because you don't want to lose your progress.
If you can accept that "risk", though, the game is interesting.

Bought this game when its name still made sense and the devs were still updating it. We're now well past the 6 month "early access" window, the game can still be beat in about 4 hours once you get past the clunky controls and there's just not a lot to do as the business management sim is fairly mindless with no option to increase difficulty nor any need to buy more than a handful of movies

Maybe I would have recommended it in November but not even a whisper of updates since October and I see HOGO Games has moved onto their next "X Simulator <current year>" game rather than finishing this one

Would love to flip this review around after a future update but currently I'm concerned they're chasing hype trains and hoping to use their studio to pump out AI slop rather than put in the work required to let this game reach its full potential

Edit: True to my word, I played again after the 2026-Aug update. The drive-thru restaurant is a step in the right direction and the pirated movies, while not compelling, at least shows an effort but it's not enough for me to flip my recommendation

Ultimately, I'd like to see the game lean more aggressively into its management sim side rather than just being another clunky physics engine where you stock shelves. This means much better UI on the menus (sorting and filtering options at least), more variable cost expenses and both the ability and a reason to sell/fire unprofitable purchases/employees

Side-note: I'm 95% sure the online ticketing feature doesn't do anything besides take a huge chunk of your capital

I really cannot recommend this game. Yes its an Early Access title, still doesn't give it a free pass however.

It runs like hell, performance is maneagable (as much as it is, considering its UE5) and only runs decently if you turn down the settings to anything below Medium. It looks good, yeah but that's the only qualifying factor it has. You can slog through a long tutorial session that's pointlessly 'voice-acted' by a generic Elevenlabs AI script, or you can go on about your way and not do them. Honestly, not doing the tutorial is preferrable. Its got really good grounds for a nice game, but only in the future because right now, it should be avoided.

The game most likely gets way better past the tutorial and the first starting area (which i heavily doubt), but it's not worth the 23€, which even then i felt like i was being robbed considering it was on sale. You can get better games with that pricetag, like; STALKER. Or, The Alters. Hell, go on moddb and get Stalker Anomaly (or GAMMA if you prefer endless torture). Mod either of them, and you have a way better experience than Dreadzone. GOG also offers the service of setting either one up for you for free.

It's saddening to know that for every 1 good game, 20 slop pieces follow like its a cross-country hike. And especially using AI to account for the ''game's general vibes'' is such a lazy excuse.

Need voice actors? Go into a closet or an enclosed space, grab your phone, record some lines; and edit them in FLStudio. It really is not that difficult.

Need art? Plenty of cheap but good artists exist in the world. There are thousands of Telegram channels, Discord servers, & Twitter feeds that have artist hubs where you can hire background artists to make simple but extravagant pieces of work for under 100€. Which shouldn't even be an issue, with the price tag that's been set.

The game needs work, a lot of work before its even acceptable to list it at the current price. I can understand listing it with the price if you are in need of funding, but then state that fact in the main page. Keep the game in the oven for a long time before giving it the full price.
